item.title: Simplified Package and version management with mise-en-place
item.description: When working on several projects simultaneously, it can sometimes be a hassle to manage all the programming languages and tools, especially if different versions of the same tool are required. This can lead to a very confusing setup with multiple versions installed via different mechanisms, annoying environment variable handling and so on. There are several tools, which address this issue, but mise-en-place especially struck my eye as it covers all my needs and is straightforward to install and use. In this article I have collected some general guidance and hints about specific problems I encountered for some particular SDKs and terminal environments.

item.title: Starlabs Starlite 5 Review
item.description:
I Recently bought the Starlite 5, a convertible Linux Tablet from Starlabs systems, a relativly small company from the UK focusing on desinging devices specifically for Linux. In order to make a judgement if such a device fits your needs, i tried to clearly identify the usage scenarios the device would serve for me. Basically, it is supposed to serve 2 purposes for me:

  1. function as a regular tablet: I previiouly owned an android tablet (lenovo tab 10) which was cheap at the time and has aged (not very well, I might add). I used it for watching videos, browsing, reading e-books, sometimes some games. A new hyrid device should be suitable for these purposes as well.
  2. use as linux laptop for situations, where portablility is requred, e.g. when traveling or visiting relatives. It being linux, it is usable for much deeper tasks such as maintainance of servers via ssh, programming etc.

item.title: Pytest Debugging in VS Code (Kedro Project)
item.description:
Recently, I started a Machine learning projects with the Kedro Framework. Based on the example spaceflights project, kedro uses the pytest library for unit testing. For a nice development workflow, I wanted to see the following requirements fulfilled:

  • Unit testing with Pytest library
  • Import module src folder
  • Ability to debug single file

Sounds simple, but there is some specific configuration necessary to make it work…

item.title: Making Angular Internationalization work with Ionic Capacitor
item.description: In a work project, we used the built-in Angular Internationalization for our ionic app. When trying to build the native version of the app, we ran into the following issue: The web directory (/path/to/project/www) must contain an "index.html".. This is due to the fact that the index.html file is located in the respective language subfolder (e.g. www/en-US) after the angular localize feature did it’s job.

item.title: Import KeyCloak Configuration via CI/CD
item.description:
In a research project, we recently introduced the identity and access management system KeyCloak into our prototype. Since we want to deploy this setup to multiple servers (acceptance and production environments) we thought about how to transfer the KeyCloak Real Settings (Email SMTP configuration, clients, etc.) from one environment to the next. This has 3 main advantages:

  • save the time to enter the same settings again, that were already tested
  • avoid mistakes when recreating those settings
  • have the base Keycloak realm settings under version control

item.title: Restore large MongoDB backup in Docker Desktop
item.description:
Recently, I wanted to restore a MongoDB backup of a bigger production database locally for testing.

The container was created with a standard docker run command: docker run -d -p 27017:27017 -v {PATH_TO_FOLDER}:/data-test -e MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME=admin -e MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD=admin --name test-mongo mongo:4.4.3.

item.title: About
item.description: In this Blog I will occasionally write about my experiences developing software during my day-job and hobby projects (im most cases it is probably clear if it was work-related or just for fun :) ).
